As an extension, we also obtain a deterministic $\tilde{O}(km^{1+o(1)}+k^5n)$-time algorithm for minimum-cost maximum-cardinality packing of $k$ forests in undirected graphs. In particular, this finds $k$ edge-disjoint spanning trees of minimum total cost, if they exist. The previous fastest algorithm takes $\tilde{O}(kn^2+m)$ time (Gabow and Westermann, 1992).

papers.title: Strict unimodality without log-concavity for partial Petrial polynomials
papers.abstract: For a simple graph $G$, the partial Petrial polynomial $P_G^{\times}(z)$ enumerates all diagonal perturbations of its adjacency matrix over $GF(2)$ by rank. We derive a rooted attachment identity and apply it to the tree $R_m$ obtained by joining a new vertex to the middle vertex of each of $m$ disjoint copies of the five-vertex path. We prove that the nonzero coefficient sequence of $P_{R_m}^{\times}(z)$ is strictly unimodal for every $m\ge1$, but is log-concave if and only if $1\le m\le3$. Thus the $21$-vertex tree $R_4$ provides an explicit strictly unimodal, non-log-concave example. For $m\ge5$, the unique mode occurs at degree $\lfloor(149m+85)/32\rfloor$. More generally, for any fixed path rooted at an internal vertex, joining a new vertex to the roots of sufficiently many disjoint copies produces a tree whose partial Petrial polynomial is not log-concave.

papers.title: Adaptive pairwise preference elicitation for decision support: identifying the best alternative with fewer judgments
papers.abstract: Interactive decision support systems often require repeated preference judgments, although identifying the best alternative may not justify eliciting all \(n(n-1)/2\) pairwise comparisons. We propose ALEC (Adaptive Lexicographic Elicitation of Comparisons), which re-ranks the alternatives after each judgment and asks the first unobserved pair in the lexicographic order of the current ranking, using the Analytic Hierarchy Process as the concrete setting. Under a log-normal error model, directly comparing a contrast maximises the one-step reduction in its effective resistance. Posterior bounds on the probability of a wrong choice or of exceeding a relative-loss tolerance provide stopping rules valid under adaptive questioning, while a consistency-and-margin condition gives a deterministic certificate of agreement with the full-matrix winner. Simulations show that re-ranking is most useful in larger problems with limited budgets; ALEC outperforms Harker's original rule in most scenarios with \(n\ge11\), while under a common stopping rule it achieves higher hit-rate point estimates than the stronger Harker-log variant at a modest additional questioning cost. With a 5\% loss tolerance and a cap of \(2n\) additional comparisons, the stopping rule saves \res{prot-s06-saveadd-min}--\res{prot-s06-saveadd-max}\% of them, while among runs stopped by the bound the observed rate of losses above tolerance remains at most \res{s06-errearly-max}\%, against a nominal 10\%. ALEC therefore provides an adaptive elicitation module for decision support systems that balances decision precision against user effort.

papers.title: Connectivity in a New Bounded-Space Dynamic Model
papers.abstract: We introduce a new model for dynamic algorithms in which the algorithm has read-only oracle access to a dynamically changing input and random access to its own bounded workspace. It is a dynamic analogue of the time-space tradeoffs for static inputs studied in complexity theory, where only writable memory counts as space. We study dynamic undirected $s$-$t$ connectivity: after every edge update to an $n$-vertex graph, an algorithm with $S$ words of workspace must report whether $s$ and $t$ are connected. The graph is accessed via adjacency list queries (degree, $j$-th neighbor) or adjacency matrix queries. Our algorithms are randomized; our lower bounds hold for randomized algorithms with $cn$ bits of workspace, $c>0$ a small constant ($cn/\log n$ for the worst-case matrix bound). We prove: (1) With adjacency lists, worst-case time $\tildeΘ(n^2/S^2)$ per insertion is necessary and sufficient for incremental algorithms. (2) With an adjacency matrix, worst-case time $\tildeΩ(n^2/S)$ per insertion is necessary for incremental algorithms, and sufficient for $S\ge\sqrt{n}$. (3) With amortization, incremental algorithms achieve $\tilde O(n/S)$ time per insertion with adjacency lists and $\tilde O(n^2/S)$ with an adjacency matrix, while $\tildeΩ(\sqrt{n/S})$ and $\tildeΩ(n\sqrt{n/S})$, respectively, are necessary. (4) Fully dynamic algorithms need amortized time $\tildeΩ(n/S)$ per update with adjacency lists and $\tildeΩ(n^2/S)$ with an adjacency matrix, even on forests, where both bounds are tight (lists: under bounded degree). Conventional dynamic connectivity admits polylogarithmic update time with $Ω(n)$ words of space. In contrast, our lower bounds show that polynomial update time is necessary whenever $S\le n^{1-\varepsilon}$, even for a single pair of vertices and even for incremental algorithms with amortized guarantees.

papers.title: Exact regions for the symmetrized Blest coefficient
papers.abstract: Spearman's rho treats all ranks alike, yet in many comparisons of two rankings an agreement at the top matters more than one at the bottom. Blest's rank correlation builds this preference into Spearman's rho, and its symmetrized version $η$, introduced by Genest and Plante, does so without favoring either of the two rankings. How far can such a top-weighted coefficient stray from other rank correlations? We answer this question for Spearman's rho, Blomqvist's beta and Chatterjee's rank correlation $ξ$ by determining the exact set of values that $η$ and each of these coefficients can attain jointly. Given Spearman's rho, $η$ can differ from it by at most $27/128$, and the extreme values of $η$ are attained only when the two rankings agree perfectly on the top ranks and are completely reversed on the bottom ranks, or vice versa. Given Blomqvist's beta, $η$ obeys exactly the same sharp bounds as Spearman's rho. For Chatterjee's rank correlation, both boundary curves are explicit and are attained by copulas with densities. Here symmetrization has a surprising effect. Compared with Blest's original coefficient, $η$ has a narrower range at fixed Spearman's rho, but near independence a wider range at fixed Chatterjee's rank correlation, where $|η|$ can come close to $\sqrt{11ξ/5}$ while Blest's coefficient stays below $\sqrt{32ξ/15}$. The proofs combine explicit Kantorovich potentials from optimal transport with a convex relaxation that turns out to be exact.

papers.title: Two-sided estimates for two-point local time tails of branching random walks: a Green function criterion
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of the joint tails of local times at two distinct sites for branching random walks (BRWs). Our principle results establish a general Green-function criterion for two-sided exponential tail bounds with a common spatial factor given by a three-point Green function convolution, and further identify a strict inequality that must be satisfied by the corresponding exponential constants. In particular, we verify this criterion for subcritical BRWs on finitely generated groups, for critical BRWs on non-elementary hyperbolic groups, and for critical BRWs on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d\geq 5$. As applications, we revisit the growth rate of visited sites on spheres in hyperbolic groups obtained by Sidoravicius et al. [Commun. Pure Appl. Math. 2023], and also establish lower bounds for the probabilities of visiting finite sets in Euclidean lattices.

papers.title: A second eigenvalue lower bound for the directed configuration model
papers.abstract: We prove a high-probability lower bound for the second eigenvalue in modulus of the transition matrix of the simple random walk on a directed configuration model with minimal out-degree at least two and maximal degree not too large. The lower bound matches the upper bound found by Coste (2021) on the same model. Our proof bypasses the need to establish convergence of the empirical eigenvalue distribution. Instead, it reduces the spectral lower bound to a central limit theorem for the trace of the transition matrix at powers much larger than the logarithmic scale, a range that previous results failed to reach. Both the general strategy and the central limit theorem might be of independent interest.

papers.title: The Spectral Theory of Cographs: A Survey, Organized by Graph Matrix
papers.abstract: Cographs, the $P_4$-free graphs, are exactly the graphs obtained from a single vertex by repeated disjoint union and complementation. They contain the threshold graphs, $\mathcal{C}$-graphs and form one of the primary areas for spectral graph theory. This survey is organized by matrix: after a preliminary section, there is one section for each of the adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, distance, eccentricity, Seidel, distance Laplacian and distance signless Laplacian matrices. Within each section we collect what is known for general cographs, for the subclass of $\mathcal{C}$-graphs, and where relevant, for threshold graphs. We highlight the results from the recent years, including the foundational work of Mohammadian et al., Jacobs et al., Ghorbani, Li et al., Niu et al., Lou et al., Wang at al., Mandal et al. Two structural facts are used throughout: every connected cograph has diameter at most $2$, which ties all four distance-type matrices to the adjacency and Laplacian matrices, and the partition of the vertex set into twin classes is equitable for every one of the eight matrices, giving a uniform description of each spectrum (for the Laplacian this is the twin-reduction theory of Barik--Reddy, which we present in detail). Besides surveying the literature, we record several consequences, and mark them as such: an exact decomposition of the eccentricity matrix of a connected cograph, yielding an eigenvalue-free interval for the eccentricity spectrum of all connected cographs; the full distance Laplacian spectrum and its extremal eigenvalues; an eigenvalue-free interval for the distance signless Laplacian valid for every connected graph of diameter at most $2$; an interlacing theorem tying the distance spectrum to the adjacency spectrum. A comparison table across all eight matrices and a list of open problems close the paper.

papers.title: Sublinear Approximations for Spanning Tree Congestion
papers.abstract: The spanning tree congestion of a connected graph \(G\) is the minimum, over all spanning trees \(T\) of \(G\), of the maximum number of edges of \(G\) crossing a cut induced by deleting an edge of \(T\). In the spanning tree congestion problem we are asked to compute a spanning tree with minimum congestion. We describe two sublinear-ratio approximation algorithms for the spanning tree congestion problem (STC): a simple $\Ot(n^{8/9})$-approximation, and a more involved $\Ot(n^{2/3})$-approximation, where the notation $\Ot$ hides factors polynomial in $\log n$.. Until now, no algorithm with sublinear ratio was known. We also prove that for any fixed $0<\varepsilon<1$, approximation of the spanning tree congestion within $2-\varepsilon$ is NP-hard. This improves the previous best known lower bound $6/5$.

papers.title: Target PageRank: Matching Prescribed PageRank Scores via Budgeted Edge Additions
papers.abstract: PageRank is widely used to quantify the importance of nodes in directed networks. In applications such as recommendation systems, it is increasingly important that the PageRank distribution provides a fair representation of node exposure. This motivates the problem of making minimal changes to a graph so that the PageRank values of a given set of target nodes $T$ match a desired vector $\boldsymbol{t}$. In this paper, we study this problem under an edge-addition budget $B$, where exactly $B$ edges may be added to the graph. We show that deciding whether a multiset of exactly $B$ added edges can make the target nodes attain their desired absolute PageRank scores is NP-complete. After this, we define the $\ell_1$ Target PageRank problem in which we seek to minimize the $\ell_1$ distance between the target vector and resultant vector. We show that this optimization problem admits no polynomial-time multiplicative constant-factor approximation unless $P=NP$. Motivated by these hardness results, we propose two greedy heuristics for approaching the target PageRank vector. We additionally propose a Random Walk Hungarian (RWH) heuristic that addresses the addition of edges between dissimilar nodes by incorporating a penalty for such edges. Finally, we evaluate the proposed heuristics on several real-world and synthetic datasets and compare their performance in terms of PageRank accuracy, computational efficiency, and the relevance of the added edges.

papers.title: Prophet Secretary for Matroids and XOS Valuations: A Separation at 1-1/e and a 0.6767 Guarantee for I.I.D. Weights
papers.abstract: Ehsani, Hajiaghayi, Kesselheim, and Singla (SODA 2018) give $(1-1/e)$-competitive algorithms for matroid prophet-secretary and prophet-secretary with XOS valuation functions. In this work we show that these two guarantees have different limits. For every matroid, we give a randomized $(1-1/e+\varepsilon_0)$-competitive algorithm, where $\varepsilon_0=10^{-6}$. The guarantee holds for independent nonnegative values with finite expected optimum. For explicitly given finite distributions with rational values and probabilities, the algorithm has polynomial worst-case running time in the matroid independence-oracle model. The oracle tests whether a queried set is independent. The algorithm makes $O(N^4)$ such queries in expectation and $O(N^4\log(N+2))$ in the worst case, where $N$ is the number of elements. We further consider the i.i.d. version of this problem and provide a $0.6767$ competitive ratio for every matroid with i.i.d.\ nonnegative weights from a known distribution. This guarantee even holds in fixed arrival order (a.k.a. i.i.d. matriod prophet inequalities), even when the algorithm learns the order only as the elements arrive. For combinatorial auctions with XOS valuations, however, we show that $1-1/e$ is the optimal competitive ratio. We give an explicit family of finite instances showing that no online algorithm can guarantee a larger competitive ratio than $1-1/e$, even when the buyers' valuations are i.i.d., every additive clause has coefficients in $\{0,1\}$, and computation is unrestricted. Thus the matroid improvement exploits structure absent from general allocation with XOS valuations.

papers.title: One-Vertex Lifts of Looped Circle Graphs: Obstructions and Interlace Polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be the adjacency matrix of a looped simple graph over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and let $t=\operatorname{diag} M$. We study the one-vertex lift with adjacency matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}M+tt^T&t\\t^T&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. A looped circle graph is called stable if its lift is a circle graph. We prove that stability is equivalent to the existence of a pseudo-orientable bouquet realizing the given looped circle graph. We then obtain a finite excluded toggle-minor characterization by applying two rooted constructions to the known excluded pivot-minors for circle graphs. An exact enumeration yields $22$ minimal toggle-equivalence classes: one of order $5$, twelve of order $6$, and nine of order $7$. The enumeration is accompanied by independently checkable linear-algebra and minor certificates. Finally, we prove $q(G^\dagger;y)=yq(G;y)$ for the vertex-nullity interlace polynomial of every looped simple graph, and derive quasi-tree counting and real determinant formulas.

papers.title: Coherent configuration on 3-uniform hypergraph over strongly regular graph
papers.abstract: This paper investigates coherent configurations on 3-uniform hypergraphs constructed from strongly regular graphs. We establish that the hypergraph preserves the automorphism group of the original graph and induces a nonhomogeneous Schurian coherent configuration. Using the case of Petersen graph, we obtain a configuration with two fibers and thirteen basic relations. We further determine their valencies and nonzero intersection numbers, together with the corresponding adjacency matrix multiplication identities.

papers.title: Occupation Measures in the ODE Method: Wasserstein Convergence and Rates
papers.abstract: We study occupation measures associated with stochastic approximation recursions within the ordinary differential equation (ODE) method. Under Lyapunov conditions ensuring that the limiting ODE has a globally exponentially stable equilibrium, we establish that the continuous-time occupation measures associated with the piecewise linear interpolation of the iterates converge almost surely in the $2$-Wasserstein topology to the Dirac mass at the equilibrium, the unique invariant probability measure of the limiting semiflow. The choice of the $2$-Wasserstein distance is naturally aligned with our continuous- and discrete-time Lyapunov drift analysis. We also consider two discrete-time sequences of occupation measures, induced by the algorithmic time scale and the iteration count, respectively, and we establish their almost sure convergence to the same invariant measure in the $2$-Wasserstein distance. We then derive corresponding convergence rates in expectation, providing a nonasymptotic complement to the almost sure results. These expectation bounds also imply some tail probability estimates. Finally, we verify that our results apply to a canonical class of linear recursions.

papers.title: Bass martingales need not stretch
papers.abstract: In classical optimal transport, the equivalence of optimality, convex gradient structure, and cyclical monotonicity is a central paradigm. Known counterexamples to this equivalence rely on carefully constructed costs. In contrast, we show that this equivalence can fail in martingale transport in dimension ${d \ge 2}$: already for the canonical martingale Benamou-Brenier problem and irreducible marginals we have the strict inclusions \[ \text{optimality} \;\subsetneq \; \text{(Bass) convex gradient structure} \;\subsetneq\; \text{martingale cyclical monotonicity}\, . \] However, under the stronger assumption of strict irreducibility, we establish that these three notions coincide. Understanding when the gradient structure guarantees optimality is also of practical relevance, since algorithms based on the Bass gradient representation are used in financial model calibration. All our counterexamples are based on the following phenomenon: for $d\ge2$, there exist two one-step martingales $X,Y$ with the same initial and terminal laws, and a convex function $ψ$ such that \[ 0=\mathbb E\big[\mathbb E[ψ(Y_1)\mid Y_0]-ψ(Y_0)\big] < \mathbb E\big[\mathbb E[ψ(X_1)\mid X_0]-ψ(X_0)\big] <\infty. \]

papers.title: Real-Space renormalization for the drawups and drawdowns of stochastic trajectories: universality classes for diffusion processes and random walks via the scale function
papers.abstract: For one-dimensional diffusion processes with arbitrary diffusion coefficient $D(x)$ and Ito force $F_I(x)$, we analyze the statistical properties of the renormalized trajectories at scale $Γ$, where one keeps only the alternating sequence of local minima and local maxima that are separated by drawups and drawdowns of amplitude bigger than $Γ$. The elementary RG-step between $Γ$ and $Γ+d Γ$ thus amounts to eliminate the drawups and drawdowns of amplitude $Γ$, a real-space-RG-procedure that is well-known for Brownian trajectories in the context of the Strong-Disorder-RG approach applied to the disorder landscape of random models. The main result is that the universality classes are determined by the scale function $s(x)$ satisfying $D(x) s''(x)+F_I(x) s'(x)=0$ that governs the exit probabilities from an interval : all the diffusions sharing the same scale function $s(x)$ have the same statistics of renormalized trajectories, even if their initial microscopic trajectories are completely different. The simplest universality classes for diffusions on the whole line $x \in ]-\infty,+\infty[$ and on the half-line $x \in ]0,+\infty[$ are illustrated with several examples of processes, with or without steady states: Cauchy, Student, Bessel, Fisher-Snedecor, Geometric Brownian. This framework concerning diffusion processes is then adapted to discrete-time and to continuous-time random walks on the one-dimensional lattice with arbitrary nearest-neighbor jump probabilities or rates.

papers.title: Graph Similarity Meets Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: A natural way to compare two graphs is to align their vertex sets by a bijection and to measure the difference of the aligned adjacency matrices in a matrix norm. Depending on the norm, this yields, for example, the edit distance, the cut distance, the spectral distance, and the local edit distance. To make these distances applicable to graphs of different order, one can consider blowups of the graphs or, equivalently, relax bijections to fractional alignments, that is, optimal transport plans between the uniform distributions on the vertex sets, in the spirit of Gromov-Wasserstein distances. We investigate how much the optimal transport versions can differ from their bijective counterparts, that is, we quantify their integrality gaps. For the edit distance, we improve the best known upper bound on the integrality gap from 3 to 2 and the lower bound from 6/5 to 4/3. For the cut distance, we approach Lovász's conjecture that $δ_\square \le 2δ_\square^{\rm OT}$ from both sides. We improve the previously best known upper bound $δ_\square \le 32 \cdot (δ_\square^{\rm OT})^{1/67}$ (Borgs, Chayes, Lovász, Sós and Vesztergombi, Adv. Math. 2008) to $δ_\square \le C_\varepsilon \cdot (δ_\square^{\rm OT})^{1-\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$, and we construct graphs $G,H$ with $δ_\square(G,H) = 2δ_\square^{\rm OT}(G,H)$, establishing a factor-2 lower bound that matches Lovász's conjecture. For the local edit and spectral distances, we obtain upper bounds of order $\sqrt{t\ln(1/t)}$ and $\sqrt{t}$, respectively, where $t$ is the corresponding optimal transport distance, and we show that, unlike for the edit and cut distances, no linear upper bounds are possible. Finally, we show that computing the optimal transport distances is NP-hard, and we give hardness of approximation results for the cut, spectral, and local edit distances.

papers.title: Degenerate McKean--Vlasov SDE with Yamada--Osgood Coefficients and Arbitrary Modulus of Continuity in Wasserstein Distance
papers.abstract: We establish the well-posedness of strong solutions for a class of degenerate mean-field stochastic differential equations with coefficients satisfying non-Lipschitz conditions. The diffusion coefficient is not required to be non-degenerate. Both the diffusion and the drift coefficients may depend on the law through the Kantorovich-Rubinstein metric with an arbitrary modulus of continuity. The drift and the diffusion satisfy a dimension-dependent Osgood-type condition, that becomes particularly sharp in dimension one. The proof combines the classical Yamada--Watanabe argument with Schauder's fixed-point theorem and does not rely on Gaussian estimates, allowing us to cover degenerate diffusions where such estimates are not available. This fills a gap in the existing literature.

papers.title: One-third Hölder stability of optimal transport maps from log-concave sources
papers.abstract: We prove quantitative stability of quadratic optimal transport maps from arbitrary log-concave sources to bounded targets. If the source $ρ$ is isotropic on $\mathbb R^d$ and the targets $μ$, $ν$ are supported in a common ball of radius $R$, their Brenier maps satisfy \[ \lVert T_μ-T_ν\rVert_{L^2(ρ)} \leqslant 17d^{2/3}R^{2/3}W_2(μ,ν)^{1/3}. \] The one-third exponent is optimal for $d\geqslant2$. The proof combines a linear stability estimate for Brenier potentials in a weighted norm with a matching weighted reverse Poincaré inequality. The weight is chosen in terms of the negative log-density of the source to account for its tails. We also show that the best dimensional constant in map stability is at least of order $d^{1/3}$.

papers.title: Relevance Propagation as Entropic Optimal Transport on Filippov Neural Networks: Sinkhorn Propagation and Region Relevance in Image Classifiers
papers.abstract: Relevance propagation, which redistributes a network's prediction backward through the layers, is usually treated as a heuristic. We show that it is the solution of a single variational problem: Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) is the divergence-free flow on the active computational graph of zero relative entropy to the backward transition law of the forward activation flow; for a non-negative reference, this is a relative entropy between Markov measures on backward paths. The rules LRP$_0$, LRP$_{z^+}$ and LRP$_{α,β}$ follow from this principle by the choice of a reference, and are instances of one rule, LRPN$_{α,β}$, whose weights may vary from node to node, for instance with the node's activity, in the spirit of Hebb's principle. The principle rests on a measure-theoretic formalization of feed-forward networks as directed acyclic graphs of Filippov operators, which covers piecewise-smooth and discontinuous architectures (e.g. hard-routed Mixture-of-Experts) with a Clarke-Filippov generalized-gradient calculus; it also characterizes backpropagation as the adjoint equation of a Lagrangian relaxation. On networks of ReLU and max-pooling nodes, LRP$_0$ is Gradient$\times$Input, with an explicit jump across a kink where LRP$_{z^+}$ stays continuous. Taking the entropy edge by edge yields a new rule, Sinkhorn Relevance Propagation. Aggregated over an input region, the flow of a non-negative reference tells, with exact accounting, which hidden units carry its evidence, the conditioned flow being a Schrödinger bridge. On VGG-16, the conservation identities hold to round-off, and the rules are told apart by the sign of their maps, the share of the output left to the bias nodes, faithfulness, localization and class dependence; on ConvNeXt-Tiny, LRPN$_{α,β}$ conserves the output and its Hebbian weights give the highest ABPC of the rules tested.

papers.title: BaCon: Band-Concentrated Exponential Random Graph Models
papers.abstract: Exponential-family random graph models ERGMs provide a parametric interpretable framework for modeling real graphs including the Web and social networks Fitted ERGMs may suffer from degeneracy matching observed graph statistics in expectation does not guarantee that the observed graph and similar ones are highly probable under the fitted distribution We introduce Band-Concentrated ERGMs BaCon a framework that avoids degeneracy by imposing a probabilistic constraint requiring at least $1-δ$ of the distribution probability mass to lie on the set of graphs with statistics within an $\varepsilon$-tolerance band around the observed statistics BaCons maximumentropy distribution still belongs to the exponential family while including a factor checking for inclusion in the tolerance band We derive the exact Metropolis-Hastings acceptance rule for this target and use a practical stochastic approximation procedure with a smoothed band membership during fitting Experiments on social networks across increasingly challenging model specifications show that BaCon substantially increases the probability mass assigned to graphs whose statistics are close to the observed ones while remaining estimable for specifications where standard ERGM estimation fails These results demonstrate that probability mass constraints are a principled way to mitigate degeneracy while retaining the benefits of exponential-family graph models

papers.title: A Random Matrix Analysis of Symmetric Tensor Unfolding
papers.abstract: We study a fundamental problem in machine learning: partial recovery of a planted signal $\boldsymbol{v} \in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ from a spiked tensor $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}} = λ\, \boldsymbol{v}^{\otimes p} + \boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$, where $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$ has symmetric Gaussian entries of variance $\asymp n^{-1}$. While previous works replace $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$ by an i.i.d. standard Gaussian tensor to circumvent technical difficulties caused by dependencies, this paper directly analyzes the symmetric model via random matrix theory. We show that the square unfolding algorithm is subject to a sharp phase transition for partial recovery at $λ\asymp n^{(p-2) / 4}$, validating an open conjecture from Montanari and Richard (2014). We get precise expressions for the limiting spectral distribution, deterministic equivalent, phase transition threshold and overlap. The main message is that unfolded symmetric tensors spectrally behave like standard Wigner matrices, up to simple transformations accounting for high-order symmetries. We consider extensions to multiple orthogonal spikes, recursive unfolding and non-square unfolding via disproportionate random matrix theory, leading to an interesting conjectured statistical-computational tradeoff regarding the choice of unfolding: square versus long.

papers.title: Logarithmic Embeddings into Probabilistic Spanning Trees for Distances and Capacities
papers.abstract: We prove that every connected $n$-vertex graph admits a probabilistic embedding into its spanning trees with expected distance stretch $O(\log n)$. This settles the logarithmic stretch conjecture of Alon, Karp, Peleg, and West, whose spanning-tree game appeared at the 1991 DIMACS Workshop on On-Line Algorithms and in SIAM Journal on Computing in 1995. A weighted form of the theorem also yields a distribution over spanning trees with capacities exactly equal to their fundamental graph cuts. Every tree dominates every graph cut, every cut is approximated within $O(\log n)$ in expectation, and the same capacity distribution defines an $O(\log n)$-competitive fractional oblivious routing. The distance and capacity distributions may differ. Diamond graphs give matching logarithmic lower bounds for stretch, congestion, and cut distortion. For rational input, both distributions are constructed deterministically in polynomial time and use at most $m$ trees, where $m$ is the number of graph edges. We prove an $Ω(m/ρ)$ support lower bound for congestion $ρ$; in particular, $(1-o(1))m$ trees can be necessary for near-unit congestion, even when the optimum tends to one. Thus linear dependence on $m$ is unavoidable in this regime. The weighted theorem combines a protected-geodesic petal decomposition with a pathwise entropy bound for locally selected centers. A local averaging inequality derandomizes the radii, and an adaptive rational packing procedure constructs the distributions.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Happy Edge Conjecture in Plane Spanning Trees
papers.abstract: We study the problem of reconfiguring plane, straight-line spanning trees on point sets in the plane. A flip is a reconfiguration step in which one edge of a tree is replaced with another, yielding again a plane spanning tree. For a given point set $P$, the flip graph has a vertex for each plane spanning tree on $P$, and an edge between any two trees that differ by a single flip. The folklore happy edge conjecture suggests that any edge shared by both the initial and the target tree (a happy edge) is never flipped in a shortest flip sequence. This conjecture was computationally verified for up to 10 points in convex position. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture both on general point sets and on point sets in convex position by providing two counterexamples on $16$ and $30$ points, respectively. The counterexample for point sets in general position also holds for compatible flips, while the happy edge property holds for compatible flips in convex point sets as shown by Aichholzer, Dorfer, and Vogtenhuber [GD 2025].

papers.title: Quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximation for exponential random graphs in the single-phase critical regime
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximations for edge-count fluctuations in dense exponential random graphs at single-phase criticality of any fixed even order $2m_*\ge 4$. The Hamiltonians use injective homomorphism counts of fixed simple graphs, with nonnegative leading coefficients for the higher-order terms. In bounded calibrated windows, edge-density fluctuations on the scale $n^{-1/m_*}$ admit an explicit non-Gaussian approximation with error $O(n^{-1/m_*})$. For parameter perturbations by fixed multiples of $n^{-1}$ with a nonzero first-order drift correction at the critical density, the deterministically centered edge count admits a Gaussian approximation on the scale $n^{(3m_*-2)/(2m_*-1)}$, with error $O(n^{-1/(2m_*-1)})$. Both rates hold in Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances. The key step is to construct auxiliary kernels for exterior graphs outside an event of exponentially small probability. These kernels contract uniformly on the full row state space and agree with the conditional Gibbs updates on typical row configurations, yielding the conditional cumulant estimates used in Stein's method.

papers.title: Incremental Minimum Spanning Trees on a Napkin
papers.abstract: In the incremental minimum spanning forest problem, weighted edges arrive one at a time. After each insertion we must report the edge that leaves the minimum spanning forest, and queries ask for the bottleneck distance of two vertices: the smallest possible maximum edge cost on a path between them. Link-cut trees solve both in $O(\log n)$ amortized time. In 2021 we wrote the folklore BottleneckTree, a short competitive-programming structure that stores one parent pointer and one cost per vertex, and conjectured that it also runs in $O(\log n)$ amortized time. We show that this conjecture is false: on a family of inputs, its amortized cost per operation is $Ω(\sqrt{n})$. We then present a structure with the same state, two arrays and a single loop, and prove that it runs in $O(\log n)$ amortized time per insertion and per query. Unlike the AM-tree of Ding, Gu and Sun, which attains the same bound, it stores no subtree sizes and maintains no balance invariant. For a connected graph with distinct costs, the structure can be viewed as an implicit link-cut tree on the Kruskal reconstruction tree: each rotation corresponds to exactly one preferred-child change, and each skip acts on a stale path-parent pointer. In experiments it is 1.3-2.1 times faster than the folklore BottleneckTree on insertions, up to 480 times faster on its adversarial input, and 6.3-16 times faster than an explicit link-cut tree.

papers.title: Testing for a Large Induced Expander: Sublinear Algorithms and Query Lower Bounds
papers.abstract: Testing expansion asks to distinguish graphs of large conductance from graphs that are far from having large conductance. We study a relaxation in which only part of the graph is required to expand: does an $n$-vertex graph of bounded degree contain an induced expander on a constant fraction of its vertices, when the rest of the graph, including the edges leaving the expander, is arbitrary? Let $P_{α,φ}$ denote the property of containing an induced subgraph on at least $αn$ vertices with inner conductance at least $φ$. For every constant $κ\in(0,1)$, we give a tester that accepts graphs in $P_{α,φ}$ and rejects graphs outside $P_{κα,μφ^2}$, where $μ=Θ_{α,κ}(1/\log n)$, using $O_{α,κ}(\sqrt n\,φ^{-2}\log n)$ queries. For fixed $α\in(0,1]$, $κ\in(0,1)$, and $0<φ\le9/20$, we further show that distinguishing these two classes requires $Ω_{α,κ,φ}(n^{1/2+c_{κ,φ}μ})$ queries for every sufficiently large $n$ and every $0<μ\le1$, where $c_{κ,φ}>0$. The bound holds for adaptive algorithms, uniformly in $μ$. Hence, for testers with $\sqrt n\,\mathrm{polylog}(n)$ queries, the logarithmic loss in conductance is necessary up to a $\log\log n$ factor. The same tester also permits distance-based rejection at a weaker conductance while retaining the original core size. Our tester compares the endpoint distributions of random walks from different vertices with each other, rather than with the uniform distribution. Its analysis uses the trace chain, which observes the walk only at its visits to the unknown expanding core. Our lower bound builds on the noisy-parity construction of [CKK+18], using vector-valued parity labels in $\mathbb F_2^r$ to create many hidden classes, each too small to contain a qualifying induced expander.

papers.title: On the one-arm probability for the metric graph Gaussian free field in high dimensions
papers.abstract: We consider the sign clusters of the Gaussian free field on the cable system of a transient weighted graph with volume growth exponent $α$ and Green function decay exponent $ν$. We prove that the probability that the cluster of a vertex reaches distance $R$ is of order $R^{-β}$ when $2α<3ν$, where $β=α-ν$ is the walk dimension, and that the same holds up to a logarithmic factor in the upper bound when $2α=3ν$. On $\mathbb Z^d$ these conditions read $d>6$ and $d=6$. The upper bound combines a general entropic bound, which compares the law of the cluster under the critical loop soup and under a massive one, with a Simon-Lieb-type inequality for the massive field derived from its Markov property. The arguments are robust and require no transitivity. The lower bound follows from a competition between the capacity and the volume of the cluster. In both bounds, the key quantity is the expected exit time of the random walk from balls, which links the volume of the cluster to its radius.

papers.title: Low moments of sums of extended Rademacher random multiplicative functions
papers.abstract: Let $X^e \colon \mathbb{N} \to \{\pm 1\}$ be the random, completely multiplicative function whose values at the primes $(X^e(p))_{p \text{ prime}}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on $\{ \pm 1 \}$. Let $X=X^eμ^2$. We determine the order of magnitude of \[ \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \bigg| \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\sum_{n \le x} X^e(n) \bigg|^{2 q} \Bigg]\quad \text{ and }\quad \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \bigg|\sum_{n \le x} \frac{X(n)}{\sqrt{n}} \bigg|^{2 q} \Bigg] \] for $q\in [0,1]$, showing that a transition from better-than-square-root cancellation to growth like a power of $\log x$ occurs when $q$ crosses $1/2$. In particular, the first absolute moments are of order $(\log\log x)^{3/4}$. The proof proceeds by comparing these sums to integrals of random Euler products, which are then studied by analogy with Gaussian multiplicative chaos integrals. The main difficulty lies in proving the lower bound at $q=1/2$, for which we also adapt arguments from the study of random walks.

papers.title: Linear Cotype Bounds for Nonlinear Spectral Gaps of Scalar Expanders
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple $d$-regular graph, $d\geq 3$, whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue satisfies $λ_2(G)\leq (1-δ)d$, where $0<δ\leq 1$. We prove that the Poincaré constant satisfies $$γ(G,\|\cdot\|_X)\lesssim \frac{qCK}δ$$ whenever $X$ is a real Banach space with a $K$-unconditional Schauder basis and cotype $q$ with constant $C$. This constant compares the mean distance over all vertex pairs with the mean distance across edges. For real Banach lattices the bound is $O(qC/δ)$. The proof estimates where a random walk first leaves each coordinate level set. As a consequence of the bound, if $n$-vertex graphs in a fixed-degree expander family embed with bounded distortion into spaces with bounded $C,K$, then $q$ must grow at least as fast as $\log n$. This order is attained in $\ell_q^n$.

papers.title: Nearly-Linear Query Algorithm for Submodular Maximization subject to a Matroid Constraint
papers.abstract: We consider monotone submodular maximization subject to a matroid constraint. The seminal continuous greedy algorithm of Calinescu, Chekuri, Pál, and Vondrák~[SICOMP'11] achieves the tight approximation of $(1-1/e)$. Since then, a line of works by Badanidiyuru and Vondrák~[SODA'14], Buchbinder, Feldman, and Schwartz~[SODA'15 \& MOR'17], Kobayashi and Terao~[ICALP'24], Buchbinder and Feldman~[FOCS'24 \& SICOMP'25], and Buchbinder and Feldman~[STOC'25] has developed efficient $(1-1/e-\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithms for this problem. We present a combinatorial randomized $(1-1/e-\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm that requires $\tilde{O}_{\varepsilon}(n)$ independence-oracle and value-oracle queries, where $n$ is the number of elements in the matroid. This is the first $(1-1/e-\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm with both independence-oracle and value-oracle query complexities nearly-linear in $n$ and polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$. To achieve this, we develop a new local search algorithm, which we call \emph{protected local search}, based on the potential function of Buchbinder and Feldman~[FOCS'24 \& SICOMP'25].

papers.title: The Maximum Second Zagreb Spectral Radius of Trees, Unicyclic Graphs and Bicyclic Graphs
papers.abstract: The second Zagreb matrix of a graph $G$ is $Z(G)=D(G)A(G)D(G)$, where $D(G)$ and $A(G)$ are the degree matrix and the adjacency matrix of $G$. For many degree-based weighted adjacency matrices, the trees, unicyclic graphs and bicyclic graphs with the largest spectral radius have a vertex adjacent to all others, and Mei et al. conjectured this for every such matrix on unicyclic graphs. Jiang et al. showed that $Z(G)$ is a counterexample. We prove that, for $q\in\{0,1,2\}$ and every $n\ge4$, the connected graph of order $n$ and cyclomatic number $q$ maximizing the spectral radius of $Z(G)$ is unique, and is obtained from two adjacent vertices with $q$ common neighbours by attaching $n-q-2$ pendent vertices to them as evenly as possible. The only exceptions are the star for $q=0$ and $n\le7$, and the triangle with one pendent vertex at each vertex for $q=1$ and $n=6$. This confirms a conjecture of Jiang et al.\ and all three parts of a conjecture of Shen and Shan for this matrix, with best possible thresholds on $n$. For $n\ge8$, the maximum value is $\lfloor (n+q)^2/4\rfloor+(n+q)/2+7q-2+O(1/n)$, whereas the star gives only $(n-1)^{3/2}$. A key tool is a determinant criterion that reduces spectral comparisons to sign conditions on explicit polynomials.

papers.title: Point interpolation and distributional universality in flow-based generative models
papers.abstract: Motivated by the expressive power of neural ordinary differential equations in flow-based generative modeling, we study the approximation of probability measures by pushforwards generated by parameterized families of Lipschitz vector fields. For Wasserstein distances, we establish a quantitative relationship between finite-sample point interpolation and distributional approximation, and derive universality criteria based on $L^p$-approximation of transport maps. In particular, affine-invariant families containing a non-affine vector field are universal from compactly supported absolutely continuous base measures. For total variation, we show that coordinate-wise dynamics are insufficient in dimensions $d\geq 2$ and establish sufficient conditions based on one-dimensional Sobolev approximation and shear-type mixing. We further examine the role of point interpolation, establishing when different regimes relate to one another and when approximate interpolation can be made exact.

papers.title: A Bayesian-Geometric Reading of Classical Model-Based Optimal Design
papers.abstract: The classical model-based optimal design criteria (D-, T-, L-, C-, and A-optimality) are usually motivated via the Cramér--Rao bound as optimizing scalar functions of the Fisher information matrix (FIM). This paper offers a complementary reading in which each criterion appears asymptotically as $N \to \infty$ as the leading-order term of an expected dissimilarity between prior and posterior, with the FIM entering through the Bernstein--von Mises limit. The Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence of the posterior relative to the prior recovers D-optimality (classically known); a reverse KL of the prior relative to the posterior recovers T-optimality (here defined as maximization of the trace of the FIM, following one common convention) and its weighted-trace generalization; and a first-order approximation of the squared 2-Wasserstein distance recovers L-, C- and A-optimality. The five criteria emerge as instances of a common Bayesian-geometric template, indexed by three choices: the dissimilarity, the prior parametrization, and the approximation scheme used to evaluate it (e.g.\ Taylor expansions of the matrix square root). For the weighted criteria, the Gaussian prior covariance encodes the criterion's weight matrix, so any choice of weights corresponds to a specific prior in the family. The T-, L-, C-, and A-optimality derivations appear novel to the best of my knowledge. A sixth criterion, E-optimality, is recovered not as an independent expected-dissimilarity limit but as a min-max robustification of C-optimality against uncertainty in the modeler's prior direction. The framework is extended to distinguish between a designer's prior over unknown parameters at design time and a modeler's prior used for posterior inference, recovering the classical expected information gain objective as a special case.

papers.title: Space-Time HWI Inequalities and the Wasserstein Current for Kinetic Equations
papers.abstract: We prove a space-time analogue of the HWI inequality of Otto-Villani for controlled kinetic equations with a semiconvex confining potential. It bounds the time-averaged relative entropy by spatial and conditional velocity transport distances, the velocity Fisher information, an intrinsic action of the path, and a boundary term given by the time endpoint values of the Wasserstein current. The key step is a differential comparison inequality for the Wasserstein current, which captures the transfer of dissipation from velocity to position. Along the Langevin semigroup, this inequality yields a kinetic evolution variational inequality involving the second time derivative of the squared spatial Wasserstein distance and a damping term. Under a compatible spatial Talagrand's transport inequality, we obtain a boundary-free space-time logarithmic Sobolev inequality on every interval $[0,T]$, $T>0$, with the optimal $T^{-2}$ short-time scaling of the constant. As a consequence, we also establish entropy decay for every friction coefficient and every initial density of finite entropy, with optimal cubic order at short times and exponential decay at long times.

papers.title: Random Walk on age-preferential random growth processes
papers.abstract: This paper studies a class of \textbf{exponentially age-preferential random growth graphs} $G(m,β)$: at each time $n$ a new vertex $v_n$ is added, and $m$ edges are drawn to existing vertices independently, with the probability that a target $v_k$ is chosen proportional to $e^{βk}$ ($β>0$), so that the graph's growth strongly favors ``young'' vertices. We systematically investigate two fundamental probabilistic problems of this model and supply the proof details: (1)~\textbf{Recurrence}: when $β>0$, the simple random walk on $G$ is recurrent with probability $1$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:rec}); (2)~\textbf{Infinite collisions}: for every $β>0$, two independent simple random walks on $G$ meet infinitely often with probability $1$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:icp}). The core of the proof is the following: by the Borel--Cantelli lemma combined with the \textbf{memoryless property} of exponential weights, $G$ is almost surely ``sausage-like'' --- there exist infinitely many bottlenecks consisting of exactly $m$ parallel edges; the cascade of bottlenecks makes the effective resistance diverge, yielding recurrence; the renewal process $\{T_k\}$ constructed at the bottleneck times has i.i.d.\ stationary increments with finite moments of every order for the first-passage times, and combined with a moderate-deviation estimate we verify Peres' Green-function criterion for infinite collisions.

papers.title: Lemmas and Conjectures in Spectral Graph Theory
papers.abstract: The corpus of Elie Duhamel and Tristan Cazenave~\cite{dc} contains $305{,}755$ automatically generated conjectures relating spectral and metric invariants of connected graphs. A pipeline generated with Claude Code (numerical refutation, proof by the SMT solver \textsf{z3} from a library of lemmas, discovery of new lemmas, formalisation in \lean~4/Mathlib) refuted $162{,}964$ conjectures and proved $117{,}390$ without any unproved hypothesis, of which $79{,}505$ are verified end to end in \lean{} for every connected graph. This document collects, with proofs written for mathematicians, the most interesting lemmas that were discovered and proved, the ten most useful lemmas, the ten hardest theorems, simpler proofs of known results (Bollobás--Erdős, Yang--Lu), and the unrefuted conjectures that we find most interesting. All the proofs are gathered in an archive

papers.title: Local limit Theorem for Directed polymers in a random environment in the full weak disorder regime
papers.abstract: For directed polymers in random environment, we provide a short and mostly self-contained proof of the local limit theorem in the full weak disorder phase, including the critical inverse temperature $β_c$. That is, the point-to-point partition function is well approximated by the product of two independent point-to-line partition functions (one starting from each endpoint of the system) multiplied by the simple random walk transition kernel. The approximation is valid in the $L^p$ sense for an optimal range of $p$. The result is new at $β=β_c$ and for $p>2$, and in all cases the proof is significantly simpler, technically and conceptually, than what can be found in the literature. As a consequence of the result we establish an invariance principle for the polymer measure with fixed end-point, valid for all $β\in [0,β_c]$.

papers.title: Expander Routing under Adversarial Deletions via Temporal Aggregation
papers.abstract: In expander routing, we seek to establish paths in the expander graph between given source-target pairs while minimizing both dilation (maximum path length) and congestion (maximum edge load). We study this problem in a decremental dynamic setting where the underlying graph remains an expander despite ongoing edge deletions, and source-target pairs can be added or removed. Our goal is to maintain paths under these updates while keeping dilation and congestion low and performing low computation per update. We present a randomized algorithm that maintains paths with polylogarithmic dilation and congestion against an adaptive adversary, while incurring only polylogarithmic amortized computation per update, all with high probability. Our approach leverages a recent technique called Temporal Aggregation to maintain a collection of low-congestion, low-dilation random walks resilient to adaptive adversaries.

papers.title: Dynamical Unbalanced Optimal Transport: Duality, Reachability, and Computation
papers.abstract: We study dynamical unbalanced optimal transport for nonlinear control-affine systems in which the control input affects both the transportation of mass and its growth or decay. This phenomenon arises naturally in controlled transport-reaction systems such as cancer treatment, and distinguishes the problem from standard unbalanced optimal transport, where transport and mass variation are typically independent. To address this problem, we combine classical relaxed-control theory with a weighted superposition principle to obtain an infinite-dimensional linear programming reformulation over weighted trajectories. Under suitable convexity and compactness assumptions, we show that this relaxation is tight. Based on the relaxation, we derive a Kantorovich dual formulation in terms of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman inequalities, and establish strong duality over smooth subsolutions. We then utilize the dual formulation to characterize reachability of the system, namely, when a given terminal measure is reachable from a given initial measure. In addition, tractable sufficient conditions for reachability are provided. Finally, we develop an augmented-Lagrangian algorithm based on the dual formulation for numerical computation of the optimal transport plan. The framework is illustrated on a phenotype-structured cancer treatment problem in which therapy simultaneously drives phenotypic adaptation and population growth or death.

papers.title: A Common Language for Dynamic Graphs: Interaction Tokenization Enables Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Dynamic graphs capture evolving interactions in Web systems, including online communication, user engagement, and recommendation. Graph foundation models aim to reuse predictive capabilities across networks, but extending this capability to dynamic graphs faces two challenges. First, node identities are graph-specific, and similar interaction patterns can appear at different temporal and activity scales, making histories difficult to represent consistently across networks. Second, the predictive roles of historical patterns vary across interaction dynamics, limiting transfer from a narrow range of training processes. In this paper, we show that a common interaction language, combined with learning across diverse interaction processes, offers a basis for dynamic graph foundation modeling. We propose CL-DGFM, a Common Language Dynamic Graph Foundation Model for temporal link prediction. Its Dynamic Interaction Tokenizer encodes interaction memory, historical connectivity, and ordered destination transitions into calibrated tabular inputs, making dynamic histories accessible to existing predictors without an additional trainable graph encoder. Its Dynamic Interaction Prior trains a pretrained tabular foundation predictor across diverse synthetic dynamics. Labeled historical context guides prediction, with a Contextual Value Adapter modulating attention values. The model transfers to real graphs without target-graph parameter updates. Experiments on TGB and TGB-Seq demonstrate competitive performance. Further comparisons show that the common language supports basic machine learning and neural models, and enables direct use of frozen tabular foundation models on dynamic graphs.

papers.title: Local scaling limit of the four-dimensional uniform spanning tree
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that the uniform spanning tree of $\mathbb Z^4$, seen from the origin, converges locally to an infinite spatial Brownian Kesten tree: a Brownian spine onto which independent spatial Brownian trees are grafted at a constant rate. The convergence holds jointly for the intrinsic metric, the volume measure and the Euclidean positions of the vertices, after rescaling these quantities by suitable constant multiples of $n^{-1}$, $n^{-2}(\log n)^{1/3}$ and $n^{-1/2}(\log n)^{-1/6}$, respectively, under the local rooted spatial Gromov-weak topology. The rescaled space-time occupation measure converges to that of infinite canonical super-Brownian motion. We also identify the limiting law of the rescaled intrinsic-ball volume and obtain sharp first-moment asymptotics.

papers.title: Mixing Time of the Random-Pair Monte Shuffle
papers.abstract: In the random-pair Monte shuffle on $n$ cards, each step chooses two positions independently and uniformly and exchanges their cards with probability $1/2$. The chosen positions are public; the decisions to exchange cards remain hidden. We prove that the mixing time in expected conditional total variation distance is $2n\log n+O(n)$, with an exact leading constant and an $O(n)$ cutoff window. To our knowledge, this is the first public-schedule Monte shuffle whose full-permutation mixing time has been determined up to an additive $O(n)$ term. The upper bound follows by comparing two executions with the same public schedule to a classical random-transposition walk. For the lower bound, we construct a schedule-dependent test function and estimate its variance using a matrix-averaging operator. Combined with the depth bound of Czumaj and Lingas, the mixing estimate gives public switching networks with at most $2n\log n+O(n)$ switches and $O(\log n)$ depth for fixed error and failure probabilities. The author obtained this result through interaction with GPT-6 Astra.

papers.title: Newtonian Dynamics in Metric Spaces
papers.abstract: We develop a variational framework for second-order, frictionless (Newtonian) dynamics in metric spaces, extending the metric theory of curves of maximal slope from gradient flows to evolutions with inertia. The construction rests on three pillars, mirroring the first-order theory. First, we introduce a class of second-order absolutely continuous curves, characterized by a geometric--variational inequality on families of tangent geodesics, and define a metric notion of acceleration. Second, we define curves of Newtonian motion as the curves achieving equality in an energy inequality involving an upper gradient--Hessian pair, which in Hilbert spaces is equivalent to Newton's equation $\ddotγ= -\nabla E(γ)$. Third, we propose a two-step predictor--corrector minimizing movement scheme and show that its discrete interpolants satisfy approximate versions of these inequalities. Under extendability and interceptor conditions on geodesics---which are satisfied, for instance, by geodesically uniformly complete, locally compact spaces with curvature bounded below---and under suitable regularity assumptions on the energy, we prove that the scheme converges, up to subsequences, to a curve of Newtonian motion. As an illustration, we recover the linear wave equation as a curve of Newtonian motion driven by the Dirichlet energy. This paper is complemented by the companion paper [Fornasier, Klemenc, Scagliotti, "A Lions Lift Framework for Gradient and Newtonian Evolutions in Wasserstein spaces"], which specifies and adapts the results to the Wasserstein metric space $(\mathcal{P}_2,W_2)$ through Lions lift, which explains Vlasov equations as Newtonian flows on spaces of probability measures.

papers.title: Reed-Muller Codes are Optimal Binary Linear 3-Query LCCs
papers.abstract: We prove that any linear $3$-query locally correctable code $C \colon \mathbb{F}_2^k \to \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with constant correction radius must have length $n \geq 2^{Ω(\sqrt{k})}$. This improves on the prior best lower bound of $2^{Ω(\sqrt{k/\log k})}$, due to [AG24], and shows that the folklore construction of linear $3$-LCCs from Reed-Muller codes, which achieve length $n = 2^{O(\sqrt{k})}$, is optimal up to constant factors in the exponent. Our proof builds on the approach of [KM24a], further refined in [Yan24,KM24b], that uses "chain derived equations" in combination with Kikuchi graphs. The crux of our argument is to show that a certain edge-coloured Kikuchi graph has a unique colour cycle: a cycle in which some colour is used exactly once. We do this by controlling the distribution of colours at each vertex in the graph using a random walk mixing argument and a novel hypergraph decomposition based on edge expansion of the hypergraph's "flattening" into a graph.

papers.title: Dynamics of Transversal Matroids
papers.abstract: We propose a way of generating matroids by randomly picking indicator vectors, and since we will see that it mostly gives uniform matroids, which are transversal, we then look at randomly generated transversal matroids. In both models we also investigate threshold phenomena of certain monotone increasing properties. Non-monotone properties of transversal matroids will also be investigated. Moreover, we are going to see how to spot circuits of a transversal matroid from its bipartite graph presentation. In the last Chapter, we have a survey of the characterization of transversal matroids that admit acyclic bipartite presentations. We will also investigate when we can simplify a presentation for a transversal matroid.

papers.title: Full-Rank Constructions of Explicit Lossless Expanders and Good Small-Set qLTCs
papers.abstract: We construct explicit two-sided lossless expanders whose binary adjacency matrices have full rank, and use them to obtain explicit asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes whose specified X- and Z-check matrices have full row rank and satisfy small-set soundness, or confinement, on a linear range. Our lossless expanders are a variant of those of Hsieh, Lubotzky, Mohanty, Reiner, and Zhang, with a free action of a finite 2-group. Under such an action, injectivity and surjectivity of the adjacency matrix are detected on a fixed-size matrix indexed by vertex orbits. Adding a sparse factor to the gadget at the middle vertices of a single type then enforces full rank, with a controlled loss in expansion. To obtain the 2-group action, we observe that reducing the generators of the Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak Ramanujan graphs modulo powers of 2, instead of modulo an odd prime, gives Ramanujan Cayley graphs on finite 2-groups. This construction may be of independent interest. Plugging two such expanders into the balanced product of Lin and Hsieh gives the quantum codes, since full rank of the input graphs is inherited by the check matrices. Our construction supplies the code family sought by Hong, Guo, and Lucas. Applying their analysis, within their framework and under their dynamical assumptions, gives quantum memories whose free-energy density is analytic at every positive temperature and whose guaranteed lifetime is $exp(Ω(N))$ at sufficiently low fixed positive temperature, where N is the blocklength. This improves the previously guaranteed stretched-exponential timescale.

papers.title: Spectral radius and size conditions for 1-tough balanced bipartite graphs to contain a $k$-factor with $k\ge 3$
papers.abstract: The largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix $A(G)$ of a graph $G$ is called the spectral radius $ρ(G)$ of $G$. If $S$ is a vertex cut of a connected graph $G$, then $c(G-S)$ denotes the number of connected components of $G-S$. The toughness $t(G)$ of a graph $G$ is defined as $t(G) = \min\left\{\frac{|S|}{c(G-S)}: S \subset V(G), \text{ and } c(G-S) > 1\right\}$. A graph \( G \) is \( t \)-tough if \( |S| \ge t c(G - S) \) for every proper subset \( S \subset V(G) \) satisfying \( c(G - S) > 1 \). Combining the toughness and spectral conditions, we provide spectral radius and size conditions for the existence of $k$-factors in 1-tough balanced bipartite graphs. This settles a problem posed by Chen, Fan and Lin in [Discrete Appl. Math. {\bf 355} (2024), 223--231].

papers.title: On a Class of Non-Local Elliptic-Transport Systems in Score-Guided Probability Flow on $SE(3)$: Score-Singularity Resolution, Space-Time ADN Shift, and Markov Mean-Field Games
papers.abstract: We establish mathematical foundations for optimal spatiotemporal vector fields governing continuous score-guided probability flows over bounded submanifolds $M \subset SE(3)$ on the Special Euclidean group $SE(3) \cong \mathbb{R}^3 \times SO(3)$. Modeling dynamic density evolution via a score-perturbed Lie-algebraic continuity equation under zero-flux boundary conditions, we resolve the non-local score drift singularity $s(g,t) = \nabla_{SE(3)} \log ρ(g,t)$ as $ρ\rightarrow 0^+$ via weighted parabolic flux dissipation bounds. Using left-invariant exponential group mollifiers, we derive boundary-preserving DiPerna--Lions commutator estimates tracking structure constants $\{c_{ij}^k\}$. Second, interpreting the optimality system as a 7D space-time elliptic operator $L_{7D} = -Δ_{SE(3)} - \partial_t^2$ with zero-order corner compatibility on $\partial M \times \{0,T\}$, we establish Agmon--Douglis--Nirenberg $W_p^2(Q_T)$ shift estimates tracking Lie algebra constants, boundary geometry $\|\partial M\|_{C^2}$, and Ricci curvature $\|Ric_{SE(3)}\|_{L^\infty}$, yielding a full $C^\infty(\overline{Q}_T)$ Schauder bootstrap expansion. Third, we extend this system to non-cooperative Markov Mean-Field Games (MFGs) on $SE(3)$, establishing score-guided Nash equilibria via Schauder--Tychonoff fixed points. Crucially, the constant diagonal Ricci curvature $Ric_{SE(3)} = \mathrm{diag}(0,0,0,1/2,1/2,1/2)$ from $SO(3)$ induces a sharp Bochner--Weitzenböck spectral gap boost $λ_1(-Δ_{SE(3)}) \ge λ_1(-Δ_{\mathbb{R}^3}) + 1/2 > 0$. This positive rotational curvature enhances the Lie-algebraic Poincaré coercivity constant, demonstrating that intrinsic group curvature stabilizes score-guided flows against dispersion and expands the critical Nash uniqueness horizon $T_{SE(3)}^*$ beyond flat Euclidean limits.

papers.title: Open problems from the Length Optimization event at MDS 2026
papers.abstract: During the Minisymposium on Length Optimization as part of the International Conference "Mathematics Days in Sofia - 2026", the participants collected the following open problems: 1. Find any non-trivial upper and lower bounds for the degree of a branching point in the Gilbert-Steiner problem with cost-function $c(x) = x^p$ in the metric space $X = \mathbb{R}^d$ for large $d$ and fixed $p > 1/2$ (see Section 1). 2. Determine whether a typical trajectory of a given branched optimal traffic plan has bounded length. To find the optimal transport plan between the Dirac measure in the center of a circle and the Lebesgue measure on the circle (see Section 2). 3. To find the maximal distance minimizers for any explicit compact sets (see Section 3). 4. What is the minimal $C$ such that for any set of $n$ points in the three-dimensional unit cube, there is a tour through all these $n$ points with the sum of the cubes of its edge lengths at most $C$ (see Section 4). 5. To explore parallels between tropical caustics and Steiner trees: do caustics really need convexity (see Section 5).

papers.title: $p$-Wasserstein distance and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish $p$-Wasserstein bounds and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk in the diffusive and critical regimes. Using a Gaussian convolution estimate with random covariance and the recursions for the conditional covariance, we obtain $W_{p,2}(\mathcal L(\widehat T_n),N(0,I_d))\le C_{a,d}pL_n$, where $\widehat T_n$ is normalized by its exact covariance and \[ L_n\asymp \begin{cases} n^{-1/2}\log n,&a\le1/3,\\ n^{-3(1/2-a)},&1/3<a<1/2,\\ (\log n)^{-3/2},&a=1/2. \end{cases} \] Consequently, we obtain radial Cramér-type moderate deviations for $x=o(L_n^{-1/3})$. We also determine the covariance bias under the uncorrected normalization and establish the corresponding Wasserstein bounds, lower bounds and moderate deviation estimates. The dimension and the model parameters are fixed.

papers.title: Precise large deviations for the elephant random walk with Weibull-type and lognormal-type random step sizes
papers.abstract: We prove precise large deviations for the symmetric elephant random walk with random step sizes. When the distribution of $|Z_1-1|$ is subexponential, we first show that, for each fixed$p\in[0,1]$, there exists a positive number sequence $b_n\to\infty$ such that \[ \mathbb P(S_n>x)\sim \mathbb P(S_n<-x)\sim \frac n2\overline F(x) \] uniformly for $x\ge b_n$, where $\overline F(x)=\mathbb P(|Z_1-1|>x)$. This existence result requires no moment assumptions and does not specify the growth rate of $b_n$. For $p\in[0,3/4]$, we further give explicit sufficient conditions on $b_n$ under Weibull-type and lognormal-type tail conditions with a regularly varying factor $x^γL(x)$, where $γ\in\mathbf R$ and $L$ is a positive measurable slowly varying function. Analogous results hold with $\mathbb P(|Z_1|>x)$ and non-strict tails.

papers.title: Volume Doubling and Geometric Inequalities on Graphs with Bakry-Émery Curvature
papers.abstract: We consider irreducible reversible Markov chains whose nonzero off-diagonal transition probabilities are bounded below by $ε>0$ and whose reversible measure satisfies $m_-\le m(x)\leκm_-$. Under the Bakry--Émery curvature condition $\mathrm{CD}(K,\infty)$, with $K\in\mathbb{R}$, we establish Wang's log-Harnack inequality $$ P_t(\log f)(x)\le\log P_tf(y) +\frac{C\mathrm{dist}(x,y)^2}{\int_0^t e^{2Ks}\mathrm{d} s}, $$ for bounded positive $f$ bounded away from zero and all $x,y\in V$, where $C$ is a constant dependent only on $\varepsilon$. Building upon this inequality, we further prove volume doubling property: let $K_-:=\max\{-K,0\}$ $$ \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,2R))\le C_0\exp\!\bigl(C_1\sqrt{K_-}\,R\bigr) \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,R)),\qquad R>0, $$ where $C_0,C_1$ depend only on $ε,κ$. If $d$ is the maximum combinatorial degree of the support graph, we further prove under $\mathrm{CD}(0,\infty)$ the sharp volume growth bound $\mathrm{Vol}(B(o,R))\le m_-CR^{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}$ for all $o$ and $R\geq 1$.

papers.title: A hitting-time version of Kotzig's conjecture in random graphs
papers.abstract: A family of perfect matchings on the same vertex set is said to have the Kotzig property if the union of any pair of matchings forms a Hamilton cycle. Kotzig famously conjectured that, when $n$ is even, the complete graph on $n$ vertices can be decomposed into $n-1$ perfect matchings with the Kotzig property. A closely related conjecture of Wormald states that, for fixed $d \ge 3$, whp a random $d$-regular graph contains $d$ perfect matchings with the Kotzig property. Recently, the first and third authors considered a version of these problems for the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$ and proved that, for every fixed $k$, there is $C=C(k)$ such that whp $G(n,C\log n/n)$ contains $k$ perfect matchings with the Kotzig property. We strengthen this result by showing a hitting time version: for every fixed $k$, whp the hitting time in the random graph process for finding $k$ edge-disjoint perfect matchings with the Kotzig property is the same as the hitting time for a graph with minimum degree $k$. This is a generalisation of the celebrated result of Bollobás and Frieze for even $n$ establishing the hitting time for $k$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles. The proof uses several ideas. We first design a coupling, via a randomised algorithm, of the random graph at the hitting time with $k$ almost-independent perfect matchings and a set of random reservoir edges, which may be of independent interest. We then prove various statistical properties of these matchings, in particular concerning the cycle structure of the $2$-factors formed by pairs of matchings. This includes a novel concept of ``shuffledness'', which we establish through a careful exposure argument and a concentration inequality for random permutations. Finally, we show that the initial $2$-factors can be merged into Hamilton cycles, using the random reservoir edges, by analysing certain Pósa-type rotations via branching processes.

papers.title: Convergence properties of nonlinear RLC electrical networks
papers.abstract: Convergence properties of general electrical networks with grounded nonlinear capacitors at the nodes and nonlinear inductors and resistors at the edges are studied. It is shown how, under appropriate conditions, for every initial condition there exists a unique equilibrium to which the system converges asymptotically. Partial extensions to networks with terminals or current sources are also provided. For RC networks this is compared with the use of an alternative storage function based on the co-content functions of the resistors.

papers.title: Covariant Calculus and Hamiltonian Flows for Nonlocal Wasserstein Metrics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study nonlocal metrics on smooth positive probability densities on a closed manifold, induced by symmetric jump kernels and density-dependent mobilities. First, we introduce the density-variation operator to express the density derivatives of the Dirichlet form and kinetic energy. Second, we construct density and velocity-field representations of the tangent space and prove their isometric equivalence. We use the generator's pseudoinverse to derive Levi-Civita connections and covariant differentials in both representations. Third, we establish mechanical Hamiltonian dynamics in both tangent representations; an action principle and Legendre duality identify the Hamilton--Jacobi and covariant Newton equations; smooth negative gradient flows admit a zero-energy Hamiltonian lift. Entropy diffusion, nonlocal mean-field equations, Keller--Segel dynamics, and a nonlocal Vlasov equation illustrate the resulting calculus. For geometric-mean mobility, the Hopf--Cole transformation of the nonlocal Schrödinger bridge system and the Madelung transformation of the nonlocal Schrödinger equation yield hyperbolic and trigonometric phase energies, respectively. At zero momentum, both recover the metric kinetic energy to second order.

papers.title: Graphs versus loopless digraphs with a given degree sequence, and convergence of uniformly random graphs at every density
papers.abstract: For a degree sequence d on n vertices with M edges, let G(d) be the number of simple graphs and D(d) the number of loopless digraphs with in-degree = out-degree = d. We conjecture that G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log(2+M/n)) for every graphical d, a single inequality across all densities, and prove it up to an extra factor log n: G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log n log(2+M/n)) for every graphical d. The proof compares pairs of graphs with Eulerian digraphs by alternately colouring closed trails; the failure of injectivity is measured exactly, shared edges cancel against 2-cycles, and parity is handled by merging trails and by a parity argument on Eulerian circuits of odd components. No asymptotic enumeration and no bound on the maximum-entropy multipliers is used. When the maximum-entropy edge probabilities lie in [delta, 1-delta], the same method gives the conjecture itself, G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log n / delta). Combined with the exact identity G(d) = exp(g*(d)) pi(d), where pi(d) is the probability that the maximum-entropy beta-model has degrees exactly d, and a van der Waerden-type bound for D(d), this shows that uniformly random graphs with degree sequence d are close in the normalized cut metric to their beta-model whenever M >> n log n log(M/n), at every density, with no tameness and no cap on the degrees. We also record the conjecture in the sparse regime and, with constant 1/2+o(1), in the dense tame regime, from the asymptotic enumerations of McKay-Wormald and Barvinok-Hartigan.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Optimization over Incomparable Spaces
papers.abstract: Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) provides a principled framework for making decisions under uncertainty when the underlying distribution may be incorrectly specified. A widely used approach builds on ideas from optimal transport (OT) as a means of measuring differences between distributions. However, this depends on these distributions residing in the same space. In certain settings, the reference data distribution we have and the space on which we make our decision may be different, which renders classical OT techniques impossible. In this paper, we provide a new DRO formulation in which ambiguity sets are defined through the Gromov-Wasserstein distance, which is an extension of OT to pairs of distributions residing in incomparable spaces. We show that several seemingly unrelated optimization formulations, including conditional value-at-risk minimization, group distributionally robust optimization, robust graph $k$-median, and $k$-median with outliers, can be recovered as special cases of our formulation. We describe the computational aspects of solving the proposed formulation based on the doubly-nonnegative relaxation. Last, we illustrate the framework through experiments on clustering over incomparable spaces and stochastic graph $k$-median.

papers.title: Fresh-Priority Eviction for Cuckoo Filters: Exploiting Latent Randomness Under XOR Hashing
papers.abstract: Cuckoo filters are a widely adopted approximate membership query (AMQ) data structure that supports insertions, lookups, and deletions with low memory overhead. At high load factors, however, insertion performance degrades sharply due to the random-walk eviction process, which may require a large number of element relocations. Recent work on bucketized cuckoo hash tables has shown that \emph{fresh-priority eviction}, which preferentially evicts elements whose alternate bucket location has not yet been used, achieves $O(\ell m)$ total expected evictions for bucket size~$\ell$, an improvement over the standard random walk. In this paper, we show that this technique transfers to \emph{cuckoo filters} despite their use of XOR-based partial-key hashing. The key insight is that a fresh element's fingerprint, although stored in the table, is not examined by the eviction policy, so when the fingerprint length satisfies $k = Ω(\log m)$, the alternate bucket hash remains a near-uniform random variable, a property we call \emph{latent randomness}. We prove that under this condition the corruption graph remains subcritical and the total number of evictions is $O(\ell m \log m)$; we conjecture the tighter $O(\ell m)$ bound holds via the full amortized analysis of Bell and Kuszmaul. We further propose encoding the fresh/kicked state implicitly by the element's position within its bucket, requiring no additional per-element metadata. Experimental results on a filter with $2^{22}$ slots and $8$-bit fingerprints demonstrate $1.2\times$ to $2.4\times$ fewer evictions at load factors between $94\%$ and $99\%$ for bucket size $\ell = 8$, and a $1.73\times$ reduction in cumulative evictions to full capacity.

papers.title: Stochastic Orders of the Exit Pair and the Monotone Response to Resetting
papers.abstract: Resetting a process, that is, restarting it from its initial position at random times, changes the probability that it leaves an interval through one end rather than the other. We show that the direction of this change is governed by how the exit time depends on the exit side, and we express this through classical stochastic orders. For random walks and birth-death chains we determine when resetting more intensively always moves the exit probability in the same direction, and we show that this can fail: we give an explicit chain in which the direction reverses twice over time, and bound the number of such reversals spectrally. We also show how the direction depends on the starting point. In the continuum limit we obtain the corresponding results for diffusions with drift.

papers.title: Approximation Algorithms for Maximum-Weight Degree-Bounded Forests
papers.abstract: In the maximum-weight degree-bounded forest problem, we are given a graph with nonnegative edge weights and a degree upper bound on each vertex. The objective is to find a maximum-weight forest satisfying the degree bounds. We show that this problem admits a simple $2$-approximation via the greedy algorithm. This already improves over the best-known guarantees obtained via a reduction to weighted $3$-matroid parity, and sets a baseline to improve upon. Our main result is an $\frac{8}{5}$-approximation algorithm for the maximum-weight degree-bounded forest problem. For the special case of uniform degree bounds, our algorithm achieves an approximation ratio of $\frac{3}{2}$. It computes two sets of edges, each of which we then restrict to a feasible solution in an optimal way, and finally returns the better of the two resulting solutions.
